stories.name: Sam Laming
stories.story_summary: Sam Laming is a professional wingsuit BASE jumper and QEST Scholar luthier (specialising in the historic English violet) who documents proximity flights through the Dolomites, Swiss Alps, Slovenian mountains, and British peaks using Insta360 cameras. His YouTube channel (Sam Laming Wingsuit) features #insta360-tagged content including 'My Scariest Wingsuit BASE jump #fail #insta360' (December 2024) and a dedicated behind-the-scenes tutorial 'How We Film a Wingsuit Jump #insta360' (August 2025), showing viewers how he captures wingsuit BASE jumps with Insta360. He became the first person to perform a close-proximity wingsuit flight over Mount Snowdon in Wales, covered by BBC. He has also appeared on Netflix and CSI, and been profiled by The Strad (classical music) as a 'Wingsuit flyer and trainee violin maker.' Previously confirmed to use Insta360 ONE X2.
stories.product_used: Insta360 (previously ONE X2; current model unconfirmed)
stories.why_it_matters: Sam Laming is one of the most genuinely multi-dimensional creators findable — a QEST Scholar luthier making baroque English violet instruments by day who BASE jumps through alpine proximity lines by night, and documents everything with Insta360. His August 2025 behind-the-scenes video 'How We Film a Wingsuit Jump #insta360' positions him as an educator for one of the most dangerous and visually spectacular creator niches in the world. He is the first person to ever fly in proximity to Snowdon, covered by BBC. He is not featured in Insta360's official creator stories, partner blog, or Team Insta360.

stories.name: Dawn Marie Dunlap
stories.story_summary: Dawn Marie Dunlap (Flying Dawn Marie) is a Southern California-based travel blogger and YouTube creator with 48K Instagram followers who reviewed the Insta360 X5 through hands-on testing at Yosemite Valley and Death Valley National Park in 2025. The review focuses on using the X5's 8K 360-degree video and 3-metre extended selfie stick to capture cinematic drone-like aerial shots in US national parks where drones are banned. Dunlap has an unusual background — she is a competitive figure skater who attended Boston University Tanglewood Institute, the Stanislavsky School at Harvard, and the American Musical and Dramatic Academy in New York — who pivoted from performing arts to travel content creation.
stories.why_it_matters: The 'drone-free national park aerial shot' angle — using Insta360's extended selfie stick + reframing to substitute for drone footage in no-drone zones — is a fresh and underserved use case that millions of national park visitors face. Dunlap reaches a specific audience (national park hikers and travel creators in NPS-regulated areas) who can't use drones and are looking for legitimate alternatives.
